assumptions: The initial offer is a contract-authorized, read-only historical audit for one independent supplier and one retailer format, using no employer data, contacts, or confidential process knowledge.
The system receives customer-authorized source data and keeps humans responsible for commercial and legal judgments; it neither impersonates customers nor determines legal entitlement.
The founder can obtain independent employment-conflict clearance and limited FMCG finance advice while remaining within the stated part-time constraint.
No unverified subscription price, recovery rate, margin, retention, or founder-wealth projection is assumed; those remain validation variables.
The intended customer has recurring deductions and a usable evidence trail that are not already resolved economically by its staff, adviser, ERP, EDI, or trade-promotion stack.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two or three contract-authorized Polish or CEE historical audits should show, against a written counterfactual, cash recovered or labor avoided that existing staff and systems would not have produced; they should also establish data completeness and permissions, a paid audit price, integration and review hours, time to value, contribution margin, a recurring budget owner, and at least one adviser-sourced repeatable acquisition path.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The sharpened insight is that value may sit not in generic invoice parsing or claims matching but in assembling permissioned, retailer-specific evidence for deductions that existing mid-market stacks leave unresolved. The historical-audit wedge makes this hypothesis testable, but the local workflow gap is supported as an inference rather than demonstrated whitespace.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Retailer deductions and investigation work are documented recurring workflows; incumbent product existence and the vendor case study support material labor and cash-flow pain. No Polish or CEE target has established recoverable value, current handling cost, budget ownership, or willingness to pay, so target-segment demand remains uncertain rather than disproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A fixed-fee audit creates a cash-first experiment, and recurring exception handling could support repeat revenue. Pricing, recoverability, acquisition cost, retention, support load, gross margin, and attribution are all unknown; connector upkeep, human review, disputed success fees, and incumbent bundling may prevent software-like economics and attractive owner earnings.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-sized CPG suppliers selling through Polish and CEE chains form a recognizable segment, and one supplier, retailer, and claim class can be a crisp initial scope. The economically meaningful subset—accounts with high recoverable leakage, usable data, and no adequate existing solution—has not been sized, while documented incumbent adoption by a 200-plus-employee producer challenges a broad underservice premise.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: SAP, HighRadius, Vistex, and Inmar already cover much or nearly all of the proposed workflow, while GS1 standards reduce normalization novelty. Regional localization and a lightweight audit may open individual accounts, but there is no proprietary access, committed channel, or evidenced underserved subsegment from which to establish a particularly strong position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If one retailer workflow succeeds, the case-file layer could extend across retailers, deduction types, suppliers, and CEE markets, then into trade-spend analytics. Each adjacency can require new permissions, mappings, evidence rules, portal maintenance, and review expertise, so expansion is plausible but not yet demonstrably low-friction.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned retailer mappings and outcome-labeled cases could create account-level workflow memory and switching friction. Transferability across customers is uncertain, standards expose core schemas, the customer controls the data, and scaled incumbents can add similar functionality; retailer-specific maintenance may be a recurring cost rather than a compounding moat.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer has no measured superiority in recovery, handling time, cost, trust, or integration ease versus staff, advisers, or incumbent suites. A localized fixed-audit entry lowers commitment, but KSeF erodes extraction differentiation and direct incumbent overlap covers the proposed full workflow.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: AI improves document matching and structured KSeF inputs lower some ingestion effort, while scrutiny of unjustified deductions may increase the value of an auditable evidence trail. KSeF also commoditizes invoice capture, and established standards and mature vendors show that this is not a newly opened category, making timing mixed.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A paid historical audit and referrals from ERP or EDI advisers are credible initial routes and fit the founder's low-public-exposure preference. No adviser has committed, the budget owner is unknown, sensitive data access requires substantial trust, and finance-system integrations can create long, costly sales and onboarding cycles.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data, AI, and FMCG-adjacent skills fit a narrow audit prototype, and a human-approval boundary limits unsafe automation. Authorized data access, employment conflicts, finance and legal judgment, changing portals, security, dispute deadlines, and retailer-specific maintenance are substantial; scalable part-time execution within the planning cap remains uncertain.

highest_value_structural_change: Replace the broad claims exchange with a productized, fixed-fee recovery audit and recurring exception module for one retailer and one high-value deduction class, delivered through an ERP or EDI adviser using customer-exported authorized data. Add persistent connectors and broader workflow only after measured incremental recovery and conversion, reducing upfront integration, access, and service risk while preserving the evidence-control point.
main_structural_strength: The offer targets a concrete cash-control point where joining promotion terms, remittance detail, and proof evidence can turn an opaque deduction into an auditable recovery case, and the historical-audit wedge can measure that value before a broad build.
primary_score_limiter: There is no demonstrated customer subset in which meaningful unrecovered deductions, complete and authorized data, adequate budget, and a genuine gap in existing staff or incumbent systems coexist; that missing intersection constrains economics, acquisition, and the attainable competitive position simultaneously.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: HighRadius explicitly markets portal and EDI capture, item-level promotion matching, external POS joins, evidence assembly, dispute submission, and ERP updates—nearly the proposed flow—while the Vistex case documents an integrated incumbent serving a 200-plus-employee food producer, directly weakening the claimed mid-market opening.
